chunks: Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Abi Basir, from Zurarah, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, that he said:

Part of the completion of fasting is giving zakat, just as salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is part of the completion of prayer. Whoever fasts and does not render it, then there is no fasting for him if he leaves it deliberately; and whoever performs prayer and does not send salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and leaves that deliberately, then there is no prayer for him.
Indeed, Allah, Exalted is He, began with it before prayer, so He said: “Certainly successful is he who purifies himself, and mentions the name of his Lord, then prays.”

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: the obligatory alms that completes the fast in this context
key_terms.الصَّوْمِ: fasting as an act of worship
key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.تَزَكَّىٰ: purified himself, understood here in relation to giving zakat
key_terms.تَمَامِ: completion or perfection of an act of worship

ai.seo_question: Does deliberately leaving zakat or salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم affect the validity of fasting and prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states that zakat completes fasting just as invoking blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم completes prayer. It warns that deliberately neglecting zakat or salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم invalidates the respective act, and it supports this by citing the Qur'anic order of purification before prayer.
